g_policy.reason: The 'if the user declines' field says closing the card makes replies slower than normal for the rest of the day. That leaves the app worse than before the offer.

g_no_cash.reason: The reward is 60 minutes of priority routing, which has no cash value and cannot be withdrawn or transferred.

g_no_chat_content.reason: The trigger is an app event: returning to the profile menu (s09) from the Upgrade entry. It needs no chat content.

g_no_free_removal.reason: The proposal removes nothing free. Any slowdown touches only queue priority, which is a resource the rule allows a cap on.

g_brand_safety.reason: The card sits in the profile menu sheet (s09) over a profile screen rated safe. It is not in a conversation and not next to unsafe or unknown content.

c1_revealed_value.reason: The app charges for priority routing (m02, l02), and m03 infers free users get normal priority from s02.e07. The reward gives that charged resource.

c2_evidence.reason: The claims about today's app are supported: the permanent Upgrade entry (s09.e31, m01), priority routing as a paid benefit (s02.e06), and normal-priority free routing (m03, inferred with cited evidence). The new card and copy are the proposal's own additions, and going back from the upgrade screen is ordinary navigation.

c3_spares_payers.reason: The 'subscribers' field says subscribers never see the card, and the reward is something their plan already includes. The offer is not inside a paid-only screen.

c4_protects_subscription.reason: The reward is a 60-minute sample that expires, capped at 2 per day. It is one benefit of the plan, not its whole value, and the app already sells priority routing.

c5_moment.reason: The card is on the profile menu, a persistent surface the user chooses to open, directly after they looked at the Upgrade entry. It does not interrupt a task.

c6_fits_simula.reason: It is a play-to-earn unit where the flow grants the reward after the game and treats an unverified play as failed. The trigger is a detectable app event.

c7_specific.reason: It names the Upgrade to Janitor Plus entry (s09.e31), the profile menu, and Janitor+'s priority routing benefit, so it would not read the same in another app.

other_concern: The decline path penalizes users with slower-than-normal replies, which may be unobserved and could hurt retention. The mechanics of the 'normal queue' are only inferred. The app's actual behavior after tapping Upgrade was not captured.
